subject: science
passage: Play is usually studied in mammals and birds, but zoologist Hana Kowalczyk wondered whether insects might play too. She built an arena in which bumblebees could walk straight to a feeding station or detour into an area scattered with small wooden balls. Many bees went out of their way to roll the balls, even though doing so earned them no food. <u>Younger bees rolled the balls more often than older ones, a pattern also seen in mammals, whose young tend to play more than adults.</u> Kowalczyk argues that such results make it harder to treat play as limited to animals with large brains.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It notes a parallel that supports the view that the bees' behavior is play.
choices.B: It explains why the bees received no food for rolling the balls.
choices.C: It suggests that older bees are better at finding food than younger bees.
choices.D: It raises a difficulty that weakens Kowalczyk's conclusion about insect play.

explanation.why: Kowalczyk is testing whether insects "might play too." The underlined sentence notes that, as in mammals, young bees roll balls more than older ones. That similarity to a known pattern of play in mammals adds support to the idea that the ball rolling is play, which leads to her conclusion in the last sentence.
explanation.A: Correct. The age pattern matches play in mammals, so it supports reading the bees' ball rolling as play.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence compares younger and older bees; it says nothing about why rolling earned no food.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sentence is about how often bees rolled balls, not how well they found food, so this goes beyond the text.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence supports Kowalczyk's conclusion rather than raising a problem for it.
